# One added diagonal fiber readout: bounded structural feasibility

Author: EM-FREE-CF1677, the same warm LOCAL actor, actual activity20/75. This is an **UNREVIEWED AUTHOR WORKING** record of one bounded question, not a paper, new Tool, Native record, physical law or accepted theorem. Its classification is RESULT_ONLY / COMPOSE_APPLIED: classical finite-difference and integer group-ring algebra applied to a specified additional observer. No scientific program, enumeration, symbolic solver or new external search was used. Parent Goal remains OPEN and the old real ending gate remains false.

The question was fixed locally in `FROZEN_MINIMAL_SEVENTH_OBSERVER_BOUNDED_QUESTION.json`,2158B, SHA256 `5277bd4aa828173e63f491eba3f8e5899480f8942c53381f37377fef6cd592d4`. An important timing correction is preserved here rather than rewriting that file: during initial internal direction selection, before writing that question file, I had already informally considered a diagonal translation-difference witness and its63 count. The file preceded the present exact old-model coverage check and complete formal argument, **not every informal construction thought**. This is a warm nonblind feasibility exercise, not a blind PhaseA claim. No future independent reviewer has received this construction.

## 1. The single reused object and its exact scope

The sole mathematical input object is the old fixed packet

`research_notes/FREE_X6_MARGINAL_32_20261008.json`

at Source `4212c4644827cc103fbe9e11d5082f18d1d2d332`,42009 UTF8 bytes, SHA256 `ba2bf5f0d0e568ebacd2d7d6f517d95d3d1fe7c8ef3de736accc8633df5451cf`, Git blob `4989d8ccc8278adaff8f542093e1a410152269b8`.

I previously personally obtained and consumed that whole packet during the fixed-snapshot mathematical audit, and retain the actual connector response at `/tmp/native-free-CF1677/marginal-review-three-actual-inputs.json`, array position0, field `result`. The old packet is reused from those exact bytes, with its size and SHA checked again; there is no new remote call. In this pass I personally reread its complete embedded `phase-a-freeze.md` and `proof-and-phase-b.md` for the model, sharp32/64 result, equality shape and existing-observer coverage. I did not execute its embedded certificate, import its code, or infer new mathematical validity from an old program result.

The relevant old conclusions are the fixed six-deletion-observer lower bound32 positive/negative mass, support64, and its equality classification as a signed alternating two-level six-coordinate box. My prior snapshot audit judged that fixed proof and typing valid; **current global review status of that old packet remains UNKNOWN**, and its historical `Independent review pending` field is not a claim about current global status. This use neither updates its status nor closes the old32 global continuity question. To avoid making this new result depend on an inference about global acceptance, section5 explicitly re-establishes all of the old lower-bound/equality facts used here from the stated model. That elementary proof is credited as reuse of the exact old proof, not as a new lemma discovery.

The inspected old two proof members define only the six coordinate-deletion readouts, their finite-box integer kernel, and a particular local relocation consumer. They do not define this seventh diagonal-coset readout. That is the whole bounded coverage statement: it is not a repository-wide or literature absence claim. No second mathematical source, catalogue, current working of another author, or capped hdiv/P11/PV search was opened for this question.

## 2. Exact restricted model and discriminating question

The old model explicitly chooses an anchor Cell c and a raw signed chart of the fixed native six-axis affine Cell torsor, X=c+Z^6. We use exactly that restricted occupancy model: a configuration f is a finitely supported function X→N0. The anchor is part of the observer setup, not an ontically distinguished origin; raw coordinates are not exported final Cell addresses. All state sites remain complete six-coordinate native Cells. Time is separately typed and unused here. No plane, extra native spatial dimension, dynamics, probability or physical law is inferred.

For i=1,...,6, M_i f is the sum over the coordinate-i fiber, with joint association of the other five coordinates retained, exactly as in the old object. Let

    v=(1,1,1,1,1,1).

Define one additional mathematical readout N_v f on the quotient set Z^6/Zv by

    (N_v f)([x]) = sum over k in Z of f(c+x+kv).

Every sum is finite. This quotient set indexes readout bins, not a lower-dimensional native world. Replacing the representative x changes only the summation index. This is a simultaneous six-axis integer displacement observer, not a claim that v itself is a primitive single-axis adjacency or a one-step physical move.

The question is whether the combined seven readouts (M_1,...,M_6,N_v) are injective on these finite nonnegative integer configurations. Two possible outcomes were specified: a proof of injectivity, or a finite actual collision. A secondary discrimination asks whether the new readout at least removes all old minimal32-mass collisions. We do not promise a sharp new minimal mass or nonnegative-fiber connectivity theorem.

## 3. Exact integer comparison kernel for all seven readouts

For a finite integer comparison h=f−g, use its Laurent polynomial

    P_h(X)=sum over x in Z^6 of h(c+x) X_1^x1 ... X_6^x6

in A=Z[X_1^{±1},...,X_6^{±1}]. Negative coefficients are formal occupancy differences, never negative physical occupancy. This is a finite representation because h has finite support. Define

    a_i=X_i−1  (i=1,...,6),
    b=X_1 X_2 X_3 X_4 X_5 X_6−1,
    G=b times product over i=1,...,6 of a_i.

The joint comparison kernel is exactly the principal ideal

    {P_h : M_i h=0 for all i, N_v h=0} = G A.             (1)

Here is a full elementary justification. Setting X_i=1 adds coefficients along coordinate-i fibers, so its image polynomial is exactly M_i h. Regard A as Laurent polynomials in X_i over the other five Laurent variables. After multiplying by a power of X_i, the ordinary polynomial remainder theorem shows that its evaluation kernel is (X_i−1). The compensating power is a unit, so the same kernel statement holds in A. The quotient A/(a_i) is the Laurent integer polynomial ring on the other five variables and is an integral domain; thus each a_i is prime in A.

For N_v, collapsing monomials with exponents differing by kv imposes the relation X_1...X_6=1. More explicitly, the invertible coordinate change

    Y=X_1...X_6,   X_6=Y/(X_1...X_5)

identifies A with Z[X_1^{±1},...,X_5^{±1},Y^{±1}]. Evaluating Y=1 sends the exponent x to the bin label (x_1−x_6,...,x_5−x_6), which has kernel Zv on the exponent group. Therefore its coefficient sums are exactly N_v h, and the same one-variable remainder argument gives kernel (b). Its quotient is again a Laurent integer polynomial domain, so b is prime.

The seven prime elements are distinct with no divisibility among different elements. Indeed reducing a_j modulo (a_i), for j≠i, leaves X_j−1 nonzero. Reducing b modulo (a_i) leaves the product of the other five variables minus1, also nonzero. Reducing each a_i modulo (b) leaves a nonconstant Laurent monomial minus1 in the five independent variables, again nonzero. These explicit quotient images establish the necessary nondivisibility; no general factorization theorem is assumed.

If P is divisible by all seven primes, write P=a_1 Q_1. Since a_2 divides P and does not divide a_1, primeness forces a_2 to divide Q_1. Continue through the six a_i and then b. This proves G divides P. Conversely any multiple of G lies in each of the seven evaluation kernels. This proves (1), including integer rather than merely rational spanning.

Equation(1) is a description of all finite signed comparison witnesses. It is not a Markov-basis claim, a path through nonnegative states, or a claim that the displayed generator has smallest possible mass among all its nonzero multiples. Translation corresponds to multiplication by a Laurent monomial and finite integer combination corresponds to addition, so no hidden infinite-support operation is used.

## 4. A finite seven-readout collision of mass63

Write

    A0=product over i=1,...,6 of (1−X_i),
    H=(X_1...X_6−1) A0.

Because there are six coordinate factors, A0=product_i a_i and hence H=G. It is nonzero in the integral domain A and belongs to the seven-readout kernel by(1). Equivalently, its signed occupancy is the translation by v of the old unit alternating cube minus that old cube; each of the six M_i remains zero under translation, while the N_v sum telescopes along each finite-support coset. This second explanation uses only finite sums and agrees with the Laurent calculation.

The old cube has vertices x in {0,1}^6 and coefficient (−1)^(x_1+...+x_6). Its translate has vertices v+x. These two vertex sets meet in exactly one point v: a coordinate simultaneously in {0,1} and {1,2} must be1. In A0 the coefficients at0 and v are both+1, since the number of axes is even. Thus in H the contribution at v from translated A0 is+1 and the contribution from minus A0 is−1, so they cancel completely.

The remaining two sets contain63 vertices each, with no other overlap, and every remaining coefficient is+1 or−1. Hence H has exactly126 support points and L1 norm126. Its total coefficient sum is H(1,...,1)=0. Therefore its positive and negative parts each have mass63.

Define f(c+x)=max(h(c+x),0), g(c+x)=max(−h(c+x),0) for the coefficient array h of H. These are distinct, finite, nonnegative integer occupancies, supported in the full native box {0,1,2}^6 including all its zero-occupancy Cells, each with total occupancy63. All seven readouts agree because they are additive and h is in their joint kernel. This is an explicit exact counterexample to injectivity, without enumerating the box or invoking a program.

## 5. The seventh readout nevertheless kills every old mass32 equality case

For completeness, the precise old facts needed below follow by the following same elementary slicing proof. For a formal algebraic number d of coordinate factors, let a nonzero finite integer array h have each one-coordinate sum zero. For d=1 it has at least two support points. For d>1, fix the last coordinate t. Every nonzero slice h_t still has all d−1 other one-coordinate sums zero, because the full corresponding readout retains t. By induction each nonzero slice has support at least2^(d−1). There are at least two nonzero slices: a single one would be the nonzero last-coordinate sum. Hence support(h)≥2^d. These d≤6 induction factors are a proof decomposition, not native lower-dimensional worlds.

If support(h)=2^d, exactly two last-coordinate slices occur, each with minimal support. The last-coordinate sum forces them to be negatives pointwise. Induction therefore gives h=a times the tensor product of d two-level differences, with nonzero integer a; the d=1 starting case has precisely that form. Conversely such a product has exactly2^d support. Total sum zero implies the positive and negative masses P,N are equal, and2P=sum|h|≥support(h). At d=6, P≥32. If P=32, then sum|h|=64 and support(h)≥64 force exactly64 support points and every absolute coefficient equal1; therefore a=+1 or−1. This proves the old equality form at precisely the scope needed here, without a global review-status premise.

Now let h be nonzero with the six old marginals zero and positive/negative masses both32. The equality form just re-established gives

    h = s times tensor product over i of (delta_{u_i}−delta_{w_i}),

where s=+1 or−1 and u_i≠w_i are arbitrary integer levels; adjacency is unnecessary. Its support is the64 vertices of that two-level box, with alternating signs.

A coset of Zv contains at most two such vertices. To see this, different vertices on the same coset differ by kv for nonzero integer k. Every one of their six coordinates must then differ, so the two vertices choose opposite levels in every coordinate. A third distinct vertex on the same coset would require three different values in any coordinate, impossible in a two-level box. This argument applies regardless of the signs or sizes of the level differences.

If a coset contains two vertices, their six level choices are all complemented, so their alternating coefficients differ by (−1)^6=+1. They have the same sign. If it contains one vertex, its nonzero coefficient also survives. Thus every occupied coset has a nonzero N_v h sum; cancellation within that coset is impossible. Consequently N_v h is not the zero readout. No old mass32 equality witness lies in the seven-readout kernel.

For arbitrary distinct nonnegative f,g with all seven readouts equal, the six old marginals imply equal total masses. Their signed difference h has equal positive and negative masses P. The old lower bound gives P≥32; the preceding argument rules out P=32. Therefore P≥33, and each of f,g has total mass at least33, even if a common nonnegative background is present. Section4 supplies a pair of mass63 with no common background. If μ7 denotes the least possible common mass of such a distinct pair, we have proved only

    33 ≤ μ7 ≤ 63.                                      (2)

This is a rigorous interval, not a sharpness assertion. The complete ideal description(1) does not by itself rule out smaller-L1 nonzero multiples of G, whose coefficients could cancel. No claim about the exact μ7 or all seven-readout extremizers is made.

## 6. Bounded outcome, usefulness and remaining boundary

The injectivity branch of the question is excluded by the actual finite witness. The new sensor does remove the entire old minimal32 ambiguity family, while finite ambiguity persists. This distinguishes a useful reduction in observational ambiguity from a complete repair. The exact signed comparison kernel supplies a verifiable interface for this one specified seven-observer family. All three conclusions concern the same question and are not counted as separate discoveries.

The new datum is the explicitly declared diagonal-coset map. It was not secretly inferred from native dimension alone and does not add a native plane, axis or force. The proof reuses the old equality theorem and standard group-ring/finite-difference algebra. No verified external novelty claim or new generic Tool is made; global dedup remains UNKNOWN. If a later exact source already contains this same seven-observer interface, it must be classified as REUSE rather than renamed novelty.

The remaining exact mass problem in(2), nonnegative-fiber connectivity, other observer maps, robust errors, dynamics and physical interpretation are outside this bounded pass. The previous first-hit memory models, PV no-consumer line, capped hdiv search, P11 missing actual inputs and all STOP objects are untouched. This working has no independent whole review and no remote Source or new activity event authorization. Further handling requires a real scope decision and, if retained as a mathematical result, a genuine nonauthor review; the author's selfcheck is not that vote.
